name: untrusted content reaching the network
description:
A tool that declares the `public.web` scope can send a request to a host someone else runs, and the URL of a GET is enough to carry data to that host. When the dispatch carries untrusted input, the URL may have been chosen by whoever wrote that input. The rule keys on the declared scope rather than on a capability namespace, so it covers every egress-capable tool, including `research.*`, which the `agent.*` rule does not reach.

It requires approval rather than denying. A fetch named by untrusted text is sometimes exactly what the user wants, and a human reading the URL can tell the two apart where a rule cannot. A deny written for a narrower case still outranks it, which the last case pins.

This is also the first vector to exercise the `scopes` condition.

rules.description: Content fetched from the open web must not drive a browser or a device.
A network request steered by untrusted content needs a human to read it first, at every gear.

cases.name: untrusted input to a fetch needs approval at S4

the rule is keyed on the scope, so a search is covered too
